description.narrative:
SDSN is working towards four sets of outcomes:
• Outcome 1: Successful operationalization of the Sustainable Development Goals and the international agreement to curb human-induced climate change.
• Outcome 2: A strong Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN) with National and Regional SDSNs around the world to promote solution initiatives and support the implementation of the SDGs.
• Outcome 3: Adoption of novel Solution Initiatives, including long-term pathways for transformations to sustainable development.
• Outcome 4: World-class Education on Sustainable Development for Everyone.

Examples of results achieved during 2019 and 2020 under the four outcomes for the intervention:
• Outcome 1: Successful operationalization of the Sustainable Development Goals and the international agreement to curb human-induced climate change.
The SDSNs work continues to be influential in academia and among policymakers. The Sustainable Development Report 2020 was released electronically on 30 June 2020, with significant increases in downloads and visits to the website (compared with previous editions) now also incl. the first SDG Index and Dashboards for Latin America and the Caribbean.
SDSN "Health for All" saw a dramatic uptick in activity in early 2020, as the network leveraged its global expertise in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. For instance, Professor Jeffrey Sachs was asked to lead a new initiative in partnership with the preeminent medical journal The Lancet.
• Outcome 2: A strong Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN) with National and Regional SDSNs around the world to promote solution initiatives and support the implementation of the SDGs.
SDSN networks continued to grow in number; SDSN has gone from 33 to 38 Networks since the last reporting period, and also include Kenya, Bolivia and Afghanistan. The networks coordinate SDSN's now 1,300 member institutions, which cover over 100 countries. SDSN has been focusing on consolidating these new networks in the reporting period.
SDSN Networks facilitate the diagnosis of local sustainable development challenges and measures. This collaboration has been further strengthened over the past six months, jointly organizing a series of public webinars to discuss topics such as the crises generated by the coronavirus to define new initiatives.
• Outcome 3: Adoption of novel Solution Initiatives, including long-term pathways for transformations to sustainable development.
To date, learners in over 190 countries have participated in the current library of more than 30 fully online courses. To support the SDGs and Agenda 2030, the SDSN is mobilizing Thematic Networks, and more than 1,200 university members to create educational opportunities for students and practitioners of sustainable development. The SDG Academy is uniquely operated through a consortium of institutions and works with SDSN members around the world to integrate high-quality online education into universities curricula. Two new courses have been released in the reporting period and three new courses are in production, one example it a course titled "Understanding Poverty and Inequality". Seven additional courses are under discussion with partners such as ILO or Unesco.
• Outcome 4: World-class Education on Sustainable Development for Everyone.
Enrollments in this period reached 90,138 learners and 6,401 verified learners, which should be added to the total cumulative enrolments since the SDG Academy began of 280,000 learners. The numbers enrolling in the Academy increased largely during the COVID-19 stay-at-home period (March 17 to June 30). Enrollments in this period, compared with the same period in 2019, proved to be 3.2x greater for overall learners and 3.9x greater for verified learners. An average of 146 countries are now represented in each course, with a continued SDSN commitment to increase the number and ensuring open access to the content globally, particularly in least developed countries.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
